This logically implies: $x(3, 4, 2) \neq \neg x(0, 2, 0)$, or equivalently, $x(3, 4, 2) = x(0, 2, 0)$.

*   Condition 28 maps to raw index 1: $(\neg x(3, 4, 2) \lor x(0, 2, 0))$

From 25 & 29: We must have $x(3, 4, 2) \land x(2, 5, 1)$ (from $x(3,4,2) \lor x(2,5,1)$ and $\neg x(3,4,2) \lor \neg x(2,5,1)$ implies equality).
